minutes.headline: Zoning Board approved a special permit for a veterinary clinic at 324 Electric Avenue, with hours and a stockade fence condition.
minutes.summary: The board heard a single application: a special permit for a veterinary clinic and hospital in a former salon unit at 324 Electric Avenue. The architect, the building owner and a neighbor spoke; no opposition was heard. The board approved the permit with set hours and a condition to put up the stockade fence, then adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a special permit for a veterinary clinic and hospital at 324 Electric Avenue.
The permit sets hours of Monday to Friday 8 to 7, Saturday 8 to 4, and closed Sunday, with a condition to put up the stockade fence.
No opposition was heard; a neighbor spoke in favor on behalf of the neighborhood and disclosed a financial interest.
The applicant will return later with a sign proposal rather than seek sign relief at this hearing.
The chair read the standard terms: town clerk filing, a 20-day appeal period, recording at the Registry of Deeds, and lapse after two years.

why_it_matters: Abutters and nearby residents have a 20-day appeal window, and the hours and fence condition set what the clinic may do next to neighboring properties.
The permit lapses after two years if unused, and signage is still undecided, so a separate sign proposal will come before the board.
watch_next: The 20-day appeal period after the decision is filed with the town clerk.
A sign proposal from the applicant at a later hearing.
